description:
A constructor field of the wrong type raises ArgumentError, identically on interp, run and build. So does <> on a non-binary.

Today (develop 37c5473cd, compiler.md C2, C17):
- <<x::8>> with x = :a
  - run: Rust panic "cannot read raw i64 from non-integer value" (the audit also saw SIGSEGV 139)
  - interp: internal error "an integer bit field expects an integer"
- <<1.5::8>>
  - run: silently gives <<0>>
  - interp: internal error
- <<x::binary>> with x an atom: non-unwinding panic, "binary/bits bit field expects heap bitstring" (ir_runtime.rs:737)
- <<x::binary-size(2)>> with "a": panic "field exceeds source" (:751)
- <<x::binary>> with x a non-binary bitstring
  - run: trap, exit 132
  - interp: "missed an exhaustive dispatch"
- <> on a non-binary raises FunctionClauseError. Elixir raises ArgumentError.

Elixir raises ArgumentError in every case above.

Fix: one contract for binary-expected and integer-expected fields, with one raiser shared by the runtime externs and the interpreter. Where the type is proven, no check is emitted.

TDD: a fixture with one row per bad field kind (the cases above plus float/integer/utf8 kinds), proven on all three paths against Elixir's output. This goes first among the codegen children: today these inputs crash the process instead of raising something try can catch.

Folded in from fz-mue.4 (agreed with Elixir Parity, 2026-11-18): the same raiser serves a utf field given a code point it cannot encode.
- <<cp::utf8>>, <<cp::utf16>> and <<cp::utf32>> with a surrogate (0xDC00) or a value past 0x10FFFF raise ArgumentError that try catches. Today the runtime panics "invalid codepoint" (ir_runtime.rs) on all three paths.
- The fixture carries one row per utf kind for each of the two bad values.
- /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-otp-json/punch/38_bs_utf8_construct_badarg.fz prints {:bad, :bad, {:ok, "aA"}} on interp, run and build.
- fz-mue (the json.erl port) depends on this ticket; Elixir Parity does not touch construction code.

comments.text: fz-mue.4 is folded in, by agreement of Elixir Parity and Binary Handling. Required: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-otp-json/punch/38_bs_utf8_construct_badarg.fz prints {:bad, :bad, {:ok, "aA"}} on interp, run and build. json.erl (fz-mue) depends on it.

User approved 14 pin rises (relayed by Binary Handling 2026-11-19): all the one-time price of the raise path's two Kernel bodies plus <>'s miss clause; many pins fell (the <> miss no longer reaches FunctionClauseError's wording). Next: docs, rebase, PR.
